    Interactive MSSR explorer

    Source: R/app.R
    mssr_app.Rd

    Opens a Shiny app for trying mssr() on synthetic examples or on an uploaded frame. It shows the input and the structure map side by side on the same input-pixel axes, line profiles, structural masks applied to the original data (mssr_mask()) and the fixture self-test (mssr_selftest()), and offers the structure map, the mask, a figure and a run record for download. The app calls the exported functions, so its results are the same as in R; it adds no processing of its own.

    Usage

    mssr_app(max_upload_mb = 50, ...)

    Arguments

    max_upload_mb

    Maximum upload size in megabytes.

    ...

    Passed to shiny::runApp(), for example port or launch.browser.

    Value

    The value of shiny::runApp(), invisibly; called for its side effect.

    Details

    Uploads. Delimited text (.csv comma-separated, .tsv or .txt separated by tabs or spaces; numbers only, no header), PNG (needs the png package; values as returned by png::readPNG(), scaled to 0..1) and TIFF (needs the tiff package; stored values, unscaled). Multi-channel images are not converted to gray: choose one channel. For multi-page TIFF choose a page. Files are read by the R process that runs the app (your own session when started with mssr_app()); the app sends nothing elsewhere.

    Limits. To keep the app responsive, runs whose estimated work exceeds 5e8 operations are refused; call mssr() directly for larger runs. The structure map is not a quantitative intensity, and nothing in the app implies a gain in physical resolution.

    Examples

    if (interactive()) {
  mssr_app()
}
